bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input materials supply disruption — The risk relates to single-source or dominant material suppliers which can cause disruption if they shut down. Mitigated by identifying alternate raw materials or alternate sources of supply for materials feeding critical finished products, including supply from a different geography or an alternative formulation, plus strategic supplier partnerships, inventory buffers and a structured periodic review of supply vulnerabilities, supplier capacity and inventory levels.
- Macro-economic factors - commodity inflation, currency and geopolitics — Macroeconomic risks leading to inflation in commodity prices, currency fluctuations and geopolitical situations can cause global supply chain disruptions, impacting profitability and operational efficiency. The Company monitors commodity prices, foreign exchange fluctuations and geopolitical developments, and leverages its strong brand equity to pass on cost increases.
- Counterfeiting and intellectual property infringement — Counterfeit and infringement activities carry significant risk of adverse impact on goodwill and brand reputation, consumer trust and confidence, and user safety; separately, leakage or exposure could undermine the confidentiality of the Company's IP. Mitigation spans trademark, design and copyright management, well-known trademark registrations for key brands, hard-to-copy packaging using lens effects and holograms, civil and criminal enforcement against counterfeiters, and physical/digital access controls, data loss prevention and patent filing frameworks at R&D centres and manufacturing facilities.
- Occupational safety and health at workplace, including handling of hazardous chemicals — People safety and health risk at manufacturing locations, offices, R&D centres and warehouses arises from operational hazards such as handling of hazardous material, fire, injury from moving machinery parts, chemical exposure and ergonomic hazards. Mitigated through a 'Zero Harm' goal, ISO 45001:2018 in majority of operations, Behaviour Based Safety programme, lead and lag safety KPI monitoring, engineering and administrative controls, the Happy and Healthy (HAH) Pidilite occupational health programme and periodic health checkups.
- Cyber security — Cyber-attacks, both external and internal, can impact IT infrastructure, with potential collapse of digital infrastructure affecting business applications, network and individual user assets. Mitigated by a cybersecurity framework with advanced technical controls, regular employee training, migration of critical systems and data to secure cloud environments with real-time redundancy, and governance structures overseeing cybersecurity.
- Legal and regulatory compliance — Non-compliance with applicable laws and regulations may lead to fines or penalties impacting Company reputation. Mitigated by a comprehensive compliance monitoring system across all entities, an online tool for large entities tracking notified regulatory changes, technology-enabled governance over insider trading and unpublished price sensitive information, periodic training, and periodic audits of compliance practices by the legal and compliance team and external experts.
- Plastic waste management and Extended Producer Responsibility — Risk of non-adherence to laws and regulations relating to plastic waste management. The Company aligns packaging practices with changing regulations, collaborates with multiple waste management agencies, complies 100% to EPR requirements, optimises packaging, reduces virgin plastic usage and uses Post Consumer Recycled (PCR) plastics, with pilots on reuse of rigid plastic packaging.
- Climate change — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: climate-related factors such as extreme weather events, water stress, regulatory changes and market transition risks may impact business operations and costs. Mitigated through climate risk assessments, strengthened regulatory monitoring, renewable energy adoption, water conservation, waste reduction and emissions management.
- Sustainable procurement and availability of natural resources — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as both risk and opportunity: responsible sourcing of raw materials is essential to supply continuity, regulatory compliance and long-term growth, with short-term negative (cost increase) and long-term positive (supply stability and growth) implications. Addressed through Sustainable Procurement and Supplier Diversity policies.
- Fraud — Risk emanating from inability to detect fraud that may lead to loss of the Company's assets or impact reputation. Mitigated by fraud prevention measures for key financial and business processes, proactive fraud risk assessments with data analytics, a formal whistleblower policy, an independent Ethics Committee, a zero-tolerance policy against unethical practice, and comprehensive insurance coverage.

outlook.body:
- Sustain the founder-legacy CSR and community programme in Gujarat - agriculture and horticulture development, farmer producer organisation support, water resource management, tree plantation, animal husbandry and women's self-help groups - which the Company frames as a deep-rooted commitment undertaken well before CSR became a statutory obligation rather than mere regulatory compliance.
- No change in the nature of business of the Company during the year.
- No formal dividend or capital-allocation policy statement is set out in this text. The practice evidenced by the 57th AGM notice is a two-part cash return to shareholders for FY 2025-26: confirmation of the payment of a special interim dividend already paid during the year and declaration of a final dividend on the equity shares of face value of Re. 1 each, both put to members as ordinary business. On the governance side, the Board reviews and approves management's strategic plan and business objectives and monitors the Company's strategic direction, with the Managing Director and Joint Managing Director responsible for executing corporate strategy and planning in consultation with the Board.
- Commitment to reducing freshwater and energy use, controlling greenhouse gas emissions and promoting renewable energy
- Managing waste - especially plastic packaging - through reuse, reduction and recycling, with 100% compliance to Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements, use of Post Consumer Recycled (PCR) plastics, reduction of virgin plastic usage, pilots on reuse of rigid plastic packaging and a stated commitment to the broader vision of a circular economy
- Occupational safety goal of 'Zero Harm' across the value chain, with ISO 45001:2018 adopted for safety management in the majority of operations, a Behaviour Based Safety programme and monitoring of lead and lag safety KPIs at all locations
- Occupational health programme under the theme of Happy and Healthy (HAH) Pidilite, with regular health risk assessments, workplace monitoring and periodic health checkups
- ESG metrics monitored and annual Sustainability Reports published since fiscal year 2018-19
- BRSR prepared per SEBI guidelines on a standalone basis, with Reasonable Assurance of BRSR Core attributes from M/s. KPMG Assurance and Consulting Services LLP
- Sustainable Procurement and Supplier Diversity policies adopted to enable environmentally and socially responsible sourcing and improve supply chain resilience
- Climate risk assessments carried out and regulatory monitoring strengthened, with renewable energy adoption, water conservation, waste reduction and emissions management initiatives
- Environment, Health and Safety policy with periodic risk assessments, engineering controls, employee training and inherently safe design standards for management of hazardous chemicals
- CSR effort focused on community well-being through education, women's empowerment, skill building, agriculture, water conservation and sanitation
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, and customers, with dedicated web-links, a customer care cell and a toll-free number
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: This text discloses no manufacturing capacity addition, plant commissioning, debottlenecking or capital-expenditure plan for the Company's own business. The only physical build-outs described are CSR facilities: a Plastic Granule Making Facility was successfully commissioned in Mahuva under a tripartite partnership with the Regional Commissionerate of Municipalities of Bhavnagar and Mahuva Nagar Palika, with an expert agency engaged for waste segregation, processing and recycling, and 23 Plastic Collection Centres established in Mahuva City to purchase scrap from rag pickers. In education, a new building is under construction at Parekh College for a computer engineering course under Shri Triveni Kalyan Education Trust, and approval has been received from Gujarat Technological University (GTU) and the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) to start MBA and MCA programmes from the academic year 2026-27. Specialised training capacity also runs through the Advance Centre for Woodworking and Plumbing at Ahmedabad in collaboration with Skill University, Government of Gujarat.

deepdive.thesis: Pidilite delivered a beat with 15.3% volume growth driven by urban discretionary recovery, but faces immediate margin pressure from 40-50% raw material inflation (VAM) due to West Asia conflict, mitigated by calibrated price hikes of 12-15% and strong inventory covers. The strategic swap of BuildNext for a minority stake in JSW One signals a pivot to leveraging partner scale over standalone platform building.

open.item: The Company is committed to occupational safety of all people across its value chain with a goal of 'Zero Harm', supported by ISO 45001:2018, a Behaviour Based Safety programme and monitoring of lead and lag safety KPIs across all locations.

Scale up production of Gracilaria dura seaweed seedlings to 10 lakh (from over 5 lakh already developed) so that farmers have the resources required for biomass cultivation, with Aquaagri partnered to enhance commercial viability.

Conduct second trials of new crops (makhana, blueberry, stevia and exotic Thai mango) at the Centre for Agriculture-Horticulture Development, Manar, to support recommending replication of these crops on farmers' fields.
Start MBA and MCA programmes from the academic year 2026-27, following approval received from Gujarat Technological University (GTU) and the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE).

Complete a new building under construction for a computer engineering course, as part of classroom and laboratory development at the 5 schools and Parekh College supported under Shri Triveni Kalyan Education Trust.

sk.overview: India's industrial catalyst and adsorbent ecosystem plays a critical role in enabling efficient, sustainable, and high-quality production across refining, petrochemical, chemical, fertilizer, and gas-processing industries. These materials, ranging from process-specific catalysts to high-performance adsorbents and inert ceramic support media, are essential for purification, dehydration, sulphur removal, hydro processing, cracking, and environmental compliance. meta.thesis: Pidilite delivered a beat with 15.3% volume growth driven by urban discretionary recovery, but faces immediate margin pressure from 40-50% raw material inflation (VAM) due to West Asia conflict, mitigated by calibrated price hikes of 12-15% and strong inventory covers. The strategic swap of BuildNext for a minority stake in JSW One signals a pivot to leveraging partner scale over standalone platform building.
